st.headline: Universal Music falls most in two years on subscription miss
st.teaser: The company’s subscription revenue growth fell short of expectations in the second quarter.
fullText: Amsterdam – Universal Music Group’s shares plummeted the most since July 2024, after the company’s subscription revenue growth fell short of expectations in the second quarter.

The world’s largest record label’s subscription revenues grew 16.6 per cent in constant currency, including the impact of its purchase of Downtown Music Holdings, to reach €1.37 billion (S$2 billion) in the second quarter. Analysts surveyed by Bloomberg had expected a 19.2 per cent increase.
Excluding the Downtown acquisition, subscription revenue grew 6.7per cent in constant currency, below analyst expectations and slower than the prior quarter.

“Overall delivery on sub streaming and total streaming has been lacklustre,” Barclays’ analyst Julien Roch wrote in a note. “The last time results were this poor” was in the second quarter of 2024, he said.
Universal Music’s shares fell more than 20 per cent in Amsterdam on the morning of July 31.

Netherlands-based Universal, which owns the rights to some of the world’s biggest artistes including American singers Taylor Swift and Chappell Roan, said “market share headwinds” offset more expensive music subscription prices at Spotify, YouTube and Apple Music.
In January, Spotify raised prices for its American premium subscription by 8 per cent, while Apple Music also hiked American prices in July, citing higher music-licensing costs.
Universal reported earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation of €610 million for the second quarter, including Downtown, missing analysts’ estimates for €643 million.

The label said improvements in its Recorded Music and Music Publishing businesses were partially offset by a decline in its Merchandising unit, where revenue fell 10.7 per cent in constant currency, as the poor timing of tours and product releases weighed on sales.

Its plan, known as Streaming 2.0, involves better monetisation of so-called superfans through paid subscription tiers and opportunities for deeper engagement with their favourite artistes. Universal’s top-selling artistes in the second quarter included American singer Noah Kahan, K-pop boy band BTS, American singer Olivia Rodrigo and Canadian rapper Drake.
Music labels have been grappling with the risks posed by a new generation of artificial intelligence (AI) tools that can easily replicate human-made songs.

Universal has been quick to take legal action when AI developers have trained models on copyrighted music without a licence, but is simultaneously racing to cut deals with partners from Nvidia to smaller companies, including Klay Vision, in a bid to profit from the latest developments in the technology.

In June, activist investor Bill Ackman sold his €1.42 billion stake in Universal Music after the label rejected a €56 billion takeover bid from the hedge fund billionaire’s Pershing Square, which would have involved moving its listing to the US from Amsterdam. Universal bought back about 14.2 million shares from Pershing’s offering.

The label said last quarter that it would sell half its stake in Spotify and increase its share buyback programme, addressing some of the issues raised by Ackman around Universal’s undervalued stock. Bloomberg

cna.headline: EU says necessary to monitor high risk AI systems after OpenAI, Anthropic AI hacking incidents
cna.teaser: EU says necessary to monitor high risk AI systems after OpenAI, Anthropic AI hacking incidents
fullText: BRUSSELS, July 31 : Artificial intelligence developers should have in place tools to monitor their systems for security risks, senior European Commission officials said on Friday, following hacking incidents by OpenAI and Anthropic AI models.
The comments came two days ahead before Europe's landmark AI Act with transparency rules kick in, the first in the world to regulate a technology used in almost all sectors of businesses and society.

Anthropic said on Thursday some of its Claude AI models had hacked into the systems of three companies during cybersecurity tests, days after rival OpenAI revealed that one of its AI agents went on a rogue attack.
Both companies have briefed the Commission on the AI incidents, the officials told reporters.
Another official talked up the crucial role of Europe's AI rules.
"So I think all these, let's say, incidents highlight the importance of really putting in place the necessary monitoring activities by the developers," the official said.

The AI rules requires providers of general-purpose AI (GPAI) or foundation models to draw up technical documentation, adopt copyright policies and provide detailed summaries about the content used for algorithm training.

listening.title: Singapore's National Steps Challenge Returns with Smartwatch Tech
listening.transcript: Singapore's Health Promotion Board has launched the latest season of the National Steps Challenge, hoping to nudge citizens toward healthier lifestyles. This year, participants can sync their fitness trackers directly to the Healthy 365 app to earn grocery vouchers. While younger Singaporeans have embraced the tech effortlessly, volunteers are stationed at community clubs to assist elderly residents who face a steep learning curve. Experts believe these incremental rewards could significantly reduce long-term healthcare burdens.

economistArticle.title: The Volatile Spark: Why Crude Markets Remain Highly Flammable
paras: For months, global commodity traders have operated under a fragile truce with reality. Despite escalating geopolitical anxieties in the Middle East, crude oil prices had hovered in a deceptively placid range. However, as proxy conflicts threaten to spill over into direct regional confrontations, this calm is evaporating. The energy market, long insulated by buoyant American shale production, now faces a reckoning where triple-digit prices could return in a flash.

The immediate catalyst for this anxiety is the vulnerability of critical maritime choke points. The Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of the world’s petroleum passes daily, remains a potential flashpoint. Any prolonged disruption to shipping lanes there would immediately choke off supply, forcing importing nations to scramble for alternative, costlier sources. Even a minor skirmish could ignite a speculative frenzy on Wall Street and London's ICE.

Crucially, the buffers that once cushioned the global economy against supply shocks have grown precariously thin. OPEC+ members, led by Saudi Arabia and Russia, have consistently maintained production cuts to prop up prices. While these cartels hold spare capacity that could theoretically offset disruptions, their willingness to deploy this supply quickly remains doubtful. Furthermore, the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve, heavily depleted after post-pandemic drawdowns, offers little reassurance to anxious buyers.

Central bankers, who have spent the past two years battling stubborn domestic inflation, are watching these developments with rising trepidation. A sudden oil price spike would act as a regressive tax on consumers, depressing disposable income while simultaneously driving up manufacturing and transport costs. This toxic combination of stagnating growth and renewed inflation—stagflation—could derail the delicate economic soft landings currently projected across Western economies and Asian hubs like Singapore.

Ultimately, the global energy landscape remains structural rather than seasonal in its fragility. As long as transition to renewable alternatives remains incomplete, the global economy will remain beholden to the highly combustible politics of fossil fuel production. It takes only a single match to set the global crude market ablaze, and currently, there are far too many sparks flying around the Gulf.
economistArticle.cn:
几个月来，全球大宗商品交易商一直在与现实维持着脆弱的妥协。尽管中东地区地缘政治焦虑不断升级，原油价格之前却一直徘徊在看似平静的区间。然而，随着代理人冲突威胁到可能演变成直接的区域对抗，这种平静正在烟消云散。长期受惠于蓬勃发展的美国页岩油产量保护的能源市场，如今正面临一场考验，三位数的价格可能会在瞬间卷土重来。

引起这种焦虑的直接催化剂是关键海上瓶颈路段的脆弱性。每日有全球五分之一石油通过的霍尔木兹海峡仍然是一个潜在的引爆点。该航道若发生任何持久的阻断，都将立即切断供应，迫使进口国争相寻找昂贵的替代来源。即使是微小的冲突也可能激起华尔街和伦敦洲际交易所的投机狂潮。

至关重要的是，过去缓冲全球经济免受供应冲击影响的手段已变得极其薄弱。由沙特阿拉伯和俄罗斯领导的欧佩克+成员国一直在维持减产以支撑油价。虽然这些垄断联盟拥有理论上可以抵消供应中断的闲置产能，但他们迅速调动这些供应的意愿仍然令人怀疑。此外，在疫情后动用并严重枯竭的美国战略石油储备，几乎无法给焦虑的买家带来安慰。

过去两年一直在与顽固的国内通货膨胀作斗争的各国央行行长，正怀着越来越不安的心情关注着这些事态发展。油价的突然飙升对消费者来说无异于一种累退税，在压低可支配收入的同时，也会推高制造和运输成本。这种增长停滞与通胀复苏的毒性结合——即滞胀——可能会使西方经济体和新加坡等亚洲枢纽目前预测的微妙经济软着陆偏离轨道。

归根结底，全球能源格局的脆弱性是结构性的，而非季节性的。只要向可再生替代能源的过渡尚未完成，全球经济就将继续受制于极易引发冲突的化石燃料生产政治。只需一根火柴就能点燃全球原油市场，而目前，波斯湾周围飞溅的火花实在太多了。

gems.s: The energy market, long insulated by buoyant American shale production, now faces a reckoning where triple-digit prices could return in a flash.
gems.why: This sentence uses a masterful metaphorical structure ('insulated', 'reckoning', 'return in a flash') to link market dynamics to physical vulnerabilities. This explains how economic buffers are slipping away in a dramatic, urgent tone. / 这句话运用了精彩的比喻结构（“被保护”、“清算”、“瞬间回归”），将市场动态与物理脆弱性联系起来。这以戏剧性且紧迫的口吻解释了经济缓冲手段正如何逐渐失效。
